messages:
maria-sd: heads up — running a pre-POC checklist for ACME. They want to host Redwood Private in their AWS account behind a Transit Gateway. Need quick alignment on recommended network setup and the minimal firewall rules for their SOC.

ajay-se: quick q — are they insisting on TGW (Transit Gateway) or would VPC peering be acceptable for the POC? TGW changes the hit list a bit.

maria-sd: they said TGW for multi-VPC routing (shared services + app VPCs), so TGW it is. also they asked about PrivateLink vs endpoint in our side.

chris-net: for TGW + PrivateLink combo: recommended pattern is host Redwood service behind an NLB in our account and expose as an Interface VPC Endpoint service (AWS PrivateLink). Customer creates interface endpoints in their VPCs that are routed via TGW to reach the endpoint. Keeps traffic private.

ajay-se: TL;DR network egress/allowlist for SOC: they typically want a compact set of CIDR/IPs and ports. we should list the absolutely required destinations (control plane, image registries, telemetry) and mark what is optional.

sasha-sec: +1. also call out DNS (53) and NTP (123) if their environment blocks those. and any KMS/HSM endpoint traffic if they plan to use a managed CMK.

chris-net: here’s a concise starter allowlist we give customers (replace with your NAT/egress proxy IPs if they centralize outbound):

```
# outbound from customer subnets (egress via NAT or TGW-proxy)
- TCP 443 -> redwood-controlplane.example.com (we will provide region-specific FQDNs)
- TCP 443 -> *.amazonaws.com (for ECR image pulls)
- TCP/UDP 53 -> your DNS resolver (or 8.8.8.8 if allowed)
- UDP 123 -> NTP servers (or your NTP infra)
- TCP 443 -> telemetry and metrics endpoints (we provide endpoints per deployment)
- TCP 443 -> kms.<region>.amazonaws.com if using AWS KMS integration
```

chris-net: If they want IPs instead of FQDNs, we can provide a short list of NLB IPs for the POC. For production we recommend FQDN + allowlisting via proxy or Resolver endpoints because NLB IPs can change across AZs.

maria-sd: can you add a short SG and route table snippet we can paste into their engineers? they asked for exact SG rules and an example route to the TGW.

chris-net: sure — security group for the interface endpoint (on customer's side) is simple: allow outbound HTTPS to our NLB, and inbound from your app subnets to the endpoint ENIs. Example: 

```
# Security group on customer VPC for Interface Endpoint ENIs
Type    Protocol  Port Range  Source
HTTPS   TCP       443         10.10.0.0/16   # app subnet CIDR
# and allow egress for DNS/NTP if using endpoint VPC
```

# Route table example (app subnet -> TGW attachment)
```
# in app subnet route table
0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-gateway-id (if internet egress required)
10.0.0.0/16 -> local
172.16.0.0/16 -> tgw-attach-id   # route to shared services via TGW
```

sasha-sec: add notes for IPS/IDS and firewall vendors: many enterprise firewalls inspect TLS and will require SNI or cert pinning exceptions. If they do deep TLS inspection, we need them to allow the Redwood control-plane FQDN in SNI whitelist.

ajay-se: also a callout on MTU: PrivateLink ENIs add overhead; recommend 9001 MTU only if they support jumbo frames across TGW and onprem. otherwise keep 1500 to avoid fragmentation.

maria-sd: can we give them a minimal list they can paste into a SOC ticket (one-liner allowlist)?

chris-net: yes — paste this minimal block: 

```
Allow outbound TCP 443 to: redwood-controlplane.<region>.redwood-infra.net, *.amazonaws.com (ECR), telemetry.<region>.redwood-infra.net
Allow DNS (UDP/TCP 53) and NTP (UDP 123) to your resolvers
If using AWS KMS integration, allow TCP 443 to kms.<region>.amazonaws.com
```

sasha-sec: thanks. one more: TLS mutual auth? ACME asked if we need mTLS for control-plane. we do optional mTLS for dedicated customers — note that in the POC we will use standard TLS w/ API keys; production can upgrade to mTLS and require extra firewall rules for client cert distribution.

ajay-se: follow-ups for the POC engineers: we need a) TGW attachment IDs, b) route table IDs, c) the subnets they want to place interface endpoints in, d) a contact for SOC to receive the short-lived NLB IPs (if they insist on IP blocks).

maria-sd: copying into the POC checklist I’ll send them. ajay, chris, can we sync offline if they want IP-based allowlist so you can generate the NLB IPs per-AZ?

chris-net: yep, I’ll run a quick script to pull NLB IPs and give a 24hr window IP list for the POC. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: scheduled — net-checker job queued to validate provided IPs against ACME firewall (job id: netchk-20260221-7).

maria-sd: perfect. I’ll update ACME and schedule a 30m call with their netops. thanks all. :pray:
